observation: Front, top and iso of the assembled set inspected; the three views are byte-identical to the ones inspected in the previous assembly round and this is the same inspection recorded against the current source. TOP: the 7 x 9 field is complete and correctly laid out -- two 2 x 3 belt blocks in the middle ranks, a den at the centre of each back rank with exactly three trap cells wrapped around it on the three sides that are not the board edge, and sixteen pieces in the opening position, eight white-based at the near end and eight black-based at the far end. Every tile sits square in its own cell with a visible rib of board around it; nothing overhangs a cell boundary and no two pieces touch. The six trap cells read as flat coloured plates flush with the field: at normal incidence the engraved sunburst does not show at all, so from directly above a trap is told by its colour and its recess alone. That is a real property of a 0.40 mm flat-bottomed engraving in a shadowless render and it is recorded rather than treated as a fault; the independent critic found all six traps unprompted at the product's own viewing angle. FRONT: the only things standing above the field are the sixteen pieces and the two flames of the near star. No trap tile breaks the board's skyline anywhere along it, which is the negative this revision turns on. The back rank also shows the size ladder directly -- Saturn and Jupiter tall, Mercury and Mars small, on identical discs. ISO: board, belt, both stars, all six traps, all sixteen worlds and both trays are present, in place and correctly coloured; the trays stand clear of the board with no part overlapping it. No misplaced, missing or extra parts, no proportion or size mismatch, no floating geometry and no visible intersection at any of the three views. Interference is settled by boolean rather than by render, and inspect interfere on this exact assembly returned zero clashes over 220 occurrences and 412 intersected pairs.
